templates.pattern: Four persons [P1],[P2],[P3],[P4] stand at four corners of a square with side [D1] km. [P1] is at NW, [P2] at NE, [P3] at SE, [P4] at SW. Each walks towards the centre. How far does each walk?
templates.explanation: Distance from corner to centre of square with side [D1] = ([D1]×√2)/2 = [D1]/√2

templates.pattern: In a town, roads run only North-South and East-West. [P1] is at intersection O. Post office is [D1] km North and [D2] km East. Bank is [D3] km South and [D4] km West of O. What is the road distance from post office to bank?
[P1] starts from O. Goes [D1] km North. Turns 135 degrees clockwise. Walks [D2] km. Turns 135 degrees clockwise. Walks [D3] km. In which direction is [P1] from O?
templates.explanation: North + 135° CW = South-East. SE + 135° CW = North-East direction roughly. But D2=D3 and turns are symmetric. Net effect: moving North initially, then SE then back NE. Final direction from O is North.

templates.pattern: A man walks [D1] km North-East, then [D2] km South-East, then [D3] km South-West, then [D4] km North-West. If [D1]=[D2]=[D3]=[D4], where does he end up?
templates.explanation: NE+SE+SW+NW with equal distances forms a rhombus. All N/S/E/W components cancel. Back at starting point.

templates.pattern: [P1] is facing North-East. [P2] is facing the direction which is 135° clockwise from [P1]'s direction. [P3] faces the direction that is 90° anticlockwise from [P2]. What direction does [P3] face?
templates.explanation: [P1] = NE. [P2] = NE + 135° CW = SW+45° = South. [P3] = South - 90° (ACW) = East.

templates.pattern: Five friends stand in a row facing North. [P1] is to the left of [P2]. [P3] is to the right of [P2]. [P4] is between [P1] and [P2]. [P5] is to the right of [P3]. What is the order from left to right?
templates.explanation: [P1] left of [P2]. [P4] between [P1] and [P2]. [P3] right of [P2]. [P5] right of [P3]. Order: P1-P4-P2-P3-P5.

templates.pattern: [P1] starts at O facing East. Walks [D1] km, turns left, walks [D2] km, turns left, walks [D3] km, turns left, walks [D4] km, turns left, walks [D5] km. What is the final direction [P1] faces?
templates.explanation: Start East. 4 left turns = back to East (4×90°=360°). After 4 turns facing East. Then walks [D5] km East. Still facing East.

templates.pattern: [P1] is at the origin. Walks to point A([D1] km East). Walks to B([D2] km North of A). Walks to C([D1] km West of B). Walks to D([D2] km South of C, which brings [P1] back to O). [P2] starts at O and walks directly to B. In what direction does [P2] walk?
templates.explanation: B is at E[D1]+N[D2] from O. Direction from O to B is North-East.

templates.pattern: [P1] starts from O. Goes [D1] km in direction 30° East of North (N30°E). What are the approximate North and East components? (sin30°=0.5, cos30°=0.87)
templates.explanation: N30°E means 30° from North towards East. North component=[D1]×cos30°=[D1]×0.87. East component=[D1]×sin30°=[D1]×0.5.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks in a pattern: 1 km East, 2 km North, 3 km West, 4 km South, 5 km East, 6 km North, 7 km West, 8 km South. What is [P1]'s displacement from start?
templates.explanation: Net E: 1-3+5-7=-4 (West). Net N: 2-4+6-8=-4 (South). Displacement = √(16+16)=4√2 km in South-West direction.

templates.pattern: [P1] goes [D1] km North from O. [P2] goes [D1] km East from O. [P3] is exactly midway between [P1] and [P2]. What is [P3]'s distance from O?

A UPSC candidate travels from home: [D1] km East to bus stop, [D2] km North to railway station, [D3] km West to exam centre, [D4] km North to college (after exam). At the end, how far is the college from home and in which direction?
templates.explanation: Net W=[D3-D1]. Net N=[D2+D4]. Direction=North-West. Distance=√(([D3-D1])²+([D2+D4])²)
